items.title: How much traffic can a $6 server handle? I measured it: 9,737 requests a second
items.summary: A real app on the cheapest droplet money buys: 1,117,976 requests with zero errors, 9,737/s static and 18,557/s once nginx cached the dynamic route. The limits I hit were a config default and my own arithmetic, not the hardware.

items.title: How many WebSocket connections can a $6 server hold? 99,770, and memory is the wall
items.summary: A plain Node WebSocket server on one shared vCPU held 99,770 live connections. Holding them cost 0-1% CPU; the real cost was 6.6KB of system memory each, half of it invisible to the process. The comfortable number is around 80,000.

items.title: A sticker over 15% of a QR code is fine. Erasing 0.7% of it kills the code.
items.summary: Everyone repeats that QR codes survive 30% damage. I measured it: a solid patch over 15% still scanned 99 times in 100, scattered speckle killed every level by 5%, and half a timing row - 0.7% of the modules - was fatal.
